result.rationale: In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, the diff replaces `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` with `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`. parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result object (e.g. `{success, data, error}`), not the parsed data, and that object is then written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. So the credential key becomes the wrapper object, corrupting stored credentials on every refresh.

judged_text: The refresh handler stores the entire safeParse wrapper object (`{success, data, error}` returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse) as the credential key instead of the parsed data, replacing the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` which returned the data itself. prisma.credential.update writes `{success: true, data: {...}}` into credential.key; on the next use, googleCredentials.access_token is undefined and the Google calendar integration fails for that user until the credential is manually repaired, while the refresh itself returned success.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (i.e., `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed credential data. This replaces the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` which returned the data itself. Storing the wrapper object in `credential.key` would break later usage where code expects `credential.key` to directly contain fields like `access_token`/`refresh_token`.
